summary: Morpheus leads Neo down a dark hall to a door and says he can only show it; Neo must step through. Neo reaches for the spherical handle but stops and backs away, saying this is not a good idea and that he does not believe, so there is no point. Morpheus asks what he believes in; Neo says he believes in nothing since his world was a lie. Morpheus says that is why they are here. Neo mocks the idea of being the One who saves the world. Morpheus says faith is of the heart and gut, and affirms he believes Neo is the One. Neo challenges him about the five before him; Morpheus, visibly wounded, admits he misunderstood the Oracle, thought it was all about him and that he could anoint anyone, calls himself terribly wrong, and says after the fifth he lost his way and doubted everything. He says then he saw Neo and his world changed, calls it whatever one likes, says he cannot explain it, and urges Neo to trust him. Neo, feeling a rush from Morpheus's zealot-like intensity, agrees. He grasps the handle, and it rotates before his fingers make contact. touching it, and a woman in white opens the door, greeting Neo that he is right on time.

what_changes.before: Resisting and pulling back from the door, insisting he does not believe and sees no point.
what_changes.after: Commits to stepping through, answering Morpheus's plea for trust with agreement.
what_changes.evidence: NEO: Morpheus, I don't think this is

what_changes.before: A confident guide who can only show the door, asking Neo to step through on his own.
what_changes.after: Openly asks Neo to lean on residual respect and trust him until Neo feels what he felt.
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS: Until that time all I am

what_changes.before: Implied certainty about his role in finding the One.
what_changes.after: Confesses he misread the Oracle, thought it was all about him, and was terribly wrong about the five before Neo.
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS: I believed what the Oracle told

event_hint.one_line: At the threshold of the Oracle's door, Morpheus wins Neo's trust by confessing his own past error about the prophecy.

uncertain: What the woman in white is or what lies beyond the door.
Whether 'right on time' means Neo was expected at an exact hour or simply has arrived.

minds.wants: To escape the door and the prophecy it represents — to refuse the role he feels is being forced on him without his consent.
minds.feels: A vertiginous loss of footing: everything he trusted about his old world is gone, so he has nothing solid to stand on, and the idea of being 'the One' feels like a further violation of the little autonomy he has left. Underneath the sarcasm is genuine fear of being used or deluded.
minds.shows: Deflation and mockery — blowing out his breath, physically backing away, dismissing the prophecy as 'insane' and 'unbelievable.' He performs the cynic so he doesn't have to perform the believer.
minds.basis: His hand reaches and stops, then he backs away; he insists 'I don't believe in anything anymore' and frames the prophecy as something 'some old lady' wants to tell him. His resistance is physical before it is verbal.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a zealot pushing a comforting delusion and wants Neo to be the One so Morpheus's faith is vindicated.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus's confession of having been 'terribly wrong' about five previous candidates reveals he is not protecting a flawless record but has already been shattered by doubt; Neo's model of him as a self-assured true-believer is already cracking by the end.

believes_about.belief: That not believing is a safe, stable place to stand — that if he refuses the prophecy, nothing can be demanded of him.
believes_about.wrong_because: His 'All right' shows his refusal is not a fortress but a posture; he commits on the strength of feeling a 'rush' from Morpheus, proving he is governable by exactly the faith he claims to reject.

minds.wants: To get Neo to step through the door — and, failing argument, to win him over by offering the one thing he has left: his own hard-won, confessed faith.
minds.feels: The old wound of the five failed candidates is still raw ('Every single day and night, I am haunted by their memory.'), so his certainty is not arrogance but something paid for at great cost; his intensity is the fervor of a man who has doubted everything and chosen to believe anyway.
minds.shows: First a confident guide ('I can only show you the door'), then — when Neo strikes at the five — a visible wounding he tries and fails to hide, then a strategic surrender into raw, unguarded conviction, ending with a direct plea to be trusted on credit.
minds.basis: The text states he 'Morpheus attempts to conceal the pain tearing through his heart.' and that admitting his error 'is difficult'; he shifts from doctrine ('Faith is not a matter of reasonability') to personal testimony and finally retain any regard you feel for me and believe in me.'

believes_about.belief: That Neo is 'the sixth and the last,' the One, and that one day Neo experience what I experienced and understand what I understand.'
believes_about.wrong_because: The coming events (the Oracle's actual test, Morpheus's later capture and the crew's scramble to save him) will complicate this certainty; at minimum his certainty outruns what he can demonstrate to Neo here, which is why he must fall back on trust rather than proof.

minds.wants: To admit Neo at the appointed moment and mark his arrival as expected.
minds.feels: Composed readiness — she acts as if Neo's coming was foreknown and is neither early nor late.
minds.shows: She opens the door before he touches the handle and greets him by name with 'You're right on time,' a calm that contrasts with the charged negotiation behind her.
minds.basis: The handle 'turns without him even touching it' and she is already there, greeting him by name before any introduction; the summary flags her as what lies beyond the threshold.

believes_about.belief: That he was expected — that his arrival is 'on time,' i.e., part of a design rather than a reluctant stumble.
believes_about.wrong_because: inferred: from Neo's side he has just capitulated on a 'rush' rather than conviction, so the neatness of 'right on time' sits against the messiness of how he actually got there — whether she means an exact appointment or simply that he has now arrived is left deliberately open.

connects_back: sc-082: Morpheus's claim that the Oracle told him 'I would find the One' is the exact certainty Neo now attacks by raising the five before him.
sc-082: The framing of the Oracle as a 'guide' who is not to be thought of 'in terms of right and wrong' sets up Neo's suspicion that this is all unverifiable.
sc-081-082: The ascent (blind man's nod, elevator, dark hall) builds the 'sense of inevitability' that Neo is physically resisting at the door.
sets_up: ev-021: Neo's 'All right' and the opening door deliver him into the Oracle's apartment, where she will test his perception rather than confirm his title.
ev-021: Morpheus's confessed past error and his plea to be trusted on faith establish the bond the Oracle's ambiguous prophecy will later strain.
The threshold crossing commits Neo to the path that will force him to choose, in ev-022 through ev-026, between his own safety and Morpheus's life.
dramatic_function: It converts a stalemate of disbelief into movement by having the authority figure disarm resistance through confessed fallibility — Morpheus wins trust not by being unshakeable but by showing he has already been broken and believed anyway, so that Neo's 'All right' is earned rather than coerced.
